questions.q: The data set $23,25,31,34,34,38,42,45$ is to be shown as a stem-and-leaf diagram with stems $2,3,4$. Write out the diagram, and use it to find the median.
questions.answer: Stem-and-leaf: $2\mid3\,5$; $3\mid1\,4\,4\,8$; $4\mid2\,5$ (key: $2\mid3=23$). With 8 values, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values: $34$ and $34$, so median $=34$.
questions.explanation: Stem-and-leaf: $2\mid3\,5$; $3\mid1\,4\,4\,8$; $4\mid2\,5$ (key: $2\mid3=23$). With 8 values, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values: $34$ and $34$, so median $=34$.

A class interval of width 10 contains 25 items. Find the frequency density, which is plotted on the vertical axis of a histogram.
questions.answer: Frequency density $=\frac{\mathrm{frequency}}{\mathrm{class\ width}}=\frac{25}{10}=2.5$.
questions.explanation: Frequency density $=\frac{\mathrm{frequency}}{\mathrm{class\ width}}=\frac{25}{10}=2.5$.

questions.q: The bar chart shows the number of books read by students in a reading challenge, grouped by number of books. Find the total number of students, and the modal group.
questions.target: Reading grouped frequency data from a bar chart
questions.answer: Total students $=12+28+15+5=60$. The modal group (highest bar) is $3\mathrm{-}5$ books, with 28 students.
questions.explanation: Total students $=12+28+15+5=60$. The modal group (highest bar) is $3\mathrm{-}5$ books, with 28 students.

questions.q: Using the same reading-challenge data (0-2: 12, 3-5: 28, 6-8: 15, 9-11: 5 students), find what percent of students read 6 or more books.
questions.target: Reading grouped frequency data from a bar chart
questions.answer: Students reading 6 or more books: $15+5=20$. Percent of the total 60 students: $\frac{20}{60}\times100\%\approx33.3\%$.
questions.explanation: Students reading 6 or more books: $15+5=20$. Percent of the total 60 students: $\frac{20}{60}\times100\%\approx33.3\%$.

questions.q: A data set has minimum $=8$, $Q_1=15$, median $=22$, $Q_3=30$, and maximum $=40$. State the interquartile range, and determine whether a value of $45$ would be considered an outlier if outliers are defined as values beyond $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$.
questions.answer: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=30-15=15$. Upper outlier boundary: $Q_3+1.5(IQR)=30+22.5=52.5$. Since $45<52.5$, the value $45$ would NOT be considered an outlier.
questions.explanation: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=30-15=15$. Upper outlier boundary: $Q_3+1.5(IQR)=30+22.5=52.5$. Since $45<52.5$, the value $45$ would NOT be considered an outlier.

questions.q: A data set has minimum $=5$, $Q_1=12$, median $=18$, $Q_3=27$, and maximum $=50$. State the interquartile range, and determine whether the maximum value would be considered an outlier if outliers are defined as values beyond $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$.
questions.answer: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=27-12=15$. Upper outlier boundary: $Q_3+1.5(IQR)=27+22.5=49.5$. Since the maximum value $50>49.5$, it WOULD be considered an outlier.
questions.explanation: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=27-12=15$. Upper outlier boundary: $Q_3+1.5(IQR)=27+22.5=49.5$. Since the maximum value $50>49.5$, it WOULD be considered an outlier.

questions.q: A data set has $Q_1=20$ and $Q_3=32$. Find the lower outlier boundary, defined as any value below $Q_1-1.5\times IQR$.
questions.answer: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=32-20=12$. $1.5\times IQR=1.5\times12=18$. Lower outlier boundary $=20-18=2$.
questions.explanation: $IQR=Q_3-Q_1=32-20=12$. $1.5\times IQR=1.5\times12=18$. Lower outlier boundary $=20-18=2$.

questions.q: A data set has mean $=42$, median $=38$, and mode $=35$. Describe the skewness of the distribution.
questions.answer: Since mean $>$ median $>$ mode, the distribution is positively skewed (skewed to the right), with a longer tail of higher values pulling the mean above the median.
questions.explanation: Since mean $>$ median $>$ mode, the distribution is positively skewed (skewed to the right), with a longer tail of higher values pulling the mean above the median.

questions.q: Two classes take the same test. Class A has mean $68$ and standard deviation $5$. Class B has mean $71$ and standard deviation $12$. Compare the two classes' performance and consistency.
questions.answer: Class B has a higher mean score (71 vs. 68), so on average Class B performed better. However, Class A has a much smaller standard deviation (5 vs. 12), meaning Class A's scores were more consistent/less spread out than Class B's.
questions.explanation: Class B has a higher mean score (71 vs. 68), so on average Class B performed better. However, Class A has a much smaller standard deviation (5 vs. 12), meaning Class A's scores were more consistent/less spread out than Class B's.

questions.q: Two machines fill bottles with a target volume of 500 mL. Machine X has mean fill volume $500$ mL and standard deviation $2$ mL. Machine Y has mean fill volume $498$ mL and standard deviation $8$ mL. Compare the two machines' accuracy and consistency.
questions.answer: Machine X's mean (500 mL) matches the target exactly, while Machine Y's mean (498 mL) is 2 mL below target. Machine X also has a much smaller standard deviation (2 mL vs. 8 mL), meaning its fill volumes are far more consistent. Machine X is therefore both more accurate and more consistent than Machine Y.
questions.explanation: Machine X's mean (500 mL) matches the target exactly, while Machine Y's mean (498 mL) is 2 mL below target. Machine X also has a much smaller standard deviation (2 mL vs. 8 mL), meaning its fill volumes are far more consistent. Machine X is therefore both more accurate and more consistent than Machine Y.

questions.q: This question has two parts. A delivery company records the delivery times (in minutes) for 50 packages: mean $=34$ minutes, standard deviation $=6$ minutes. Company policy states any delivery beyond 2 standard deviations above the mean is classified as late. (a) Find the delivery-time threshold, in minutes, above which a delivery is classified as late. (b) If a customer's package took 44 minutes to deliver, determine, using the standard deviation, whether this delivery should be classified as late, and state how many standard deviations from the mean this value lies.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: analyzing delivery times
questions.answer: (a) Threshold $=34+2(6)=34+12=46$ minutes. (b) $44$ minutes is $\frac{44-34}{6}=\frac{10}{6}\approx1.67$ standard deviations above the mean. Since $1.67<2$, this delivery is NOT classified as late.
questions.explanation: (a) Threshold $=34+2(6)=34+12=46$ minutes. (b) $44$ minutes is $\frac{44-34}{6}=\frac{10}{6}\approx1.67$ standard deviations above the mean. Since $1.67<2$, this delivery is NOT classified as late.

questions.q: Find all complex solutions to $z^4 + 16 = 0$ in exact rectangular form $a + bi$ using De Moivre's roots theorem.
questions.answer: Step 1: Express $-16$ in polar modulus-argument form: $z^4 = -16 = 16(\cos\pi + i\sin\pi).$ Here $r = 16$, $\theta = \pi$, and $n = 4$. Step 2: Apply n-th roots formula: $w_k = \sqrt[4]{16}\left[ \cos\left(\frac{\pi + 2\pi k}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{\pi + 2\pi k}{4}\right) \right] = 2\left[ \cos\left(\frac{(2k + 1)\pi}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{(2k + 1)\pi}{4}\right) \right], \; k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}.$ Step 3: Evaluate for each $k$:$k = 0$: $2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{2} + i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 1$: $2\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{2} + i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 2$: $2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{2} - i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 3$: $2\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{2} - i\sqrt{2}$.The four roots are $\pm\sqrt{2} \pm i\sqrt{2}$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Express $-16$ in polar modulus-argument form: $z^4 = -16 = 16(\cos\pi + i\sin\pi).$ Here $r = 16$, $\theta = \pi$, and $n = 4$. Step 2: Apply n-th roots formula: $w_k = \sqrt[4]{16}\left[ \cos\left(\frac{\pi + 2\pi k}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{\pi + 2\pi k}{4}\right) \right] = 2\left[ \cos\left(\frac{(2k + 1)\pi}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{(2k + 1)\pi}{4}\right) \right], \; k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}.$ Step 3: Evaluate for each $k$:$k = 0$: $2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{2} + i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 1$: $2\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{2} + i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 2$: $2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{2} - i\sqrt{2}$.$k = 3$: $2\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) = 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{2} - i\sqrt{2}$.The four roots are $\pm\sqrt{2} \pm i\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: The depth of water $h(t)$ in meters at a harbor entrance $t$ hours after midnight is modelled by $h(t) = 3.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 6.5$ for $0 \leq t \leq 24$. (a) State the maximum and minimum depths of water and their times of occurrence. (b) Find the period of the tidal oscillation. (c) A cargo ship requires a minimum water depth of 8.25 meters to safely enter the harbor. Find the total number of hours during the first 12 hours of the day when the ship can safely enter.
questions.answer: (a) Maximum depth occurs when $\cos = 1$: $h_{\max} = 6.5 + 3.5 = 10.0\mathrm{\ m}$. This occurs at $t = 0$, $t = 12$, and $t = 24$ hours. Minimum depth occurs when $\cos = -1$: $h_{\min} = 6.5 - 3.5 = 3.0\mathrm{\ m}$. This occurs at $t = 6$ and $t = 18$ hours. (b) Period $T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{\pi / 6} = 12\mathrm{\ hours}$. (c) Solve $h(t) \geq 8.25$ over $[0, 12]$: $3.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 6.5 = 8.25 \Rightarrow 3.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = 1.75 \Rightarrow \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = \frac{1.75}{3.5} = 0.5.$ In $[0, 2\pi]$, $\cos\theta = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{3}$. Setting $\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t_1 = 2\mathrm{\ hours}$. Setting $\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t_2 = 10\mathrm{\ hours}$. Since the cosine curve starts at a maximum at $t = 0$, the depth exceeds 8.25 m from $t = 0$ to $t = 2$ (2 hours) and from $t = 10$ to $t = 12$ (2 hours). Total safe duration in first 12 hours = $2 + 2 = 4\mathrm{\ hours}$.
questions.explanation: (a) Maximum depth occurs when $\cos = 1$: $h_{\max} = 6.5 + 3.5 = 10.0\mathrm{\ m}$. This occurs at $t = 0$, $t = 12$, and $t = 24$ hours. Minimum depth occurs when $\cos = -1$: $h_{\min} = 6.5 - 3.5 = 3.0\mathrm{\ m}$. This occurs at $t = 6$ and $t = 18$ hours. (b) Period $T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{\pi / 6} = 12\mathrm{\ hours}$. (c) Solve $h(t) \geq 8.25$ over $[0, 12]$: $3.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 6.5 = 8.25 \Rightarrow 3.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = 1.75 \Rightarrow \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = \frac{1.75}{3.5} = 0.5.$ In $[0, 2\pi]$, $\cos\theta = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{3}$. Setting $\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t_1 = 2\mathrm{\ hours}$. Setting $\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t_2 = 10\mathrm{\ hours}$. Since the cosine curve starts at a maximum at $t = 0$, the depth exceeds 8.25 m from $t = 0$ to $t = 2$ (2 hours) and from $t = 10$ to $t = 12$ (2 hours). Total safe duration in first 12 hours = $2 + 2 = 4\mathrm{\ hours}$.

questions.q: Find all vertical, horizontal, and slant asymptotes and any removable discontinuities (holes) of the rational function $f(x) = \frac{3x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 4}$. Describe its end behavior using limits.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: analyzing delivery times
questions.answer: Step 1: Domain and vertical asymptotes: The denominator factors as $x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)$. The numerator $3x^2 + 1 > 0$ has no real zeros. Thus, there are no common factors and no removable holes. The vertical asymptotes are $x = 2$ and $x = -2$. Step 2: Horizontal asymptote and end behavior: Numerator and denominator have equal degree $n = d = 2$: $\lim_{x \rightarrow \pm\infty} f(x) = \lim_{x \rightarrow \pm\infty} \frac{3 + 1/x^2}{1 - 4/x^2} = \frac{3}{1} = 3.$ The horizontal asymptote is $y = 3$. Notice that for all $|x| > 2$, $f(x) = 3 + \frac{13}{x^2 - 4} > 3$, so the graph approaches $y = 3$ from above as $x \rightarrow \pm\infty$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Domain and vertical asymptotes: The denominator factors as $x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)$. The numerator $3x^2 + 1 > 0$ has no real zeros. Thus, there are no common factors and no removable holes. The vertical asymptotes are $x = 2$ and $x = -2$. Step 2: Horizontal asymptote and end behavior: Numerator and denominator have equal degree $n = d = 2$: $\lim_{x \rightarrow \pm\infty} f(x) = \lim_{x \rightarrow \pm\infty} \frac{3 + 1/x^2}{1 - 4/x^2} = \frac{3}{1} = 3.$ The horizontal asymptote is $y = 3$. Notice that for all $|x| > 2$, $f(x) = 3 + \frac{13}{x^2 - 4} > 3$, so the graph approaches $y = 3$ from above as $x \rightarrow \pm\infty$.

questions.q: A circle with centre $O$ has radius $r = 8\mathrm{\ cm}$. Chord $AB$ subtends a central angle $\angle AOB = \frac{3\pi}{4}$ radians. (a) Find the exact length of the minor arc $AB$. (b) Find the exact area of the sector $OAB$. (c) Find the exact area of the minor segment enclosed between chord $AB$ and arc $AB$.
questions.answer: (a) Arc length: $s = r\theta = 8 \times \frac{3\pi}{4} = 6\pi\mathrm{\ cm}.$ (b) Sector area: $A_{\mathrm{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(8^2)\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 32 \times \frac{3\pi}{4} = 24\pi\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$ (c) Triangle area: $A_{\mathrm{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(64)\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 16\sqrt{2}\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$ Segment area: $A_{\mathrm{segment}} = A_{\mathrm{sector}} - A_{\mathrm{triangle}} = 24\pi - 16\sqrt{2} = 8(3\pi - 2\sqrt{2})\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$
questions.explanation: (a) Arc length: $s = r\theta = 8 \times \frac{3\pi}{4} = 6\pi\mathrm{\ cm}.$ (b) Sector area: $A_{\mathrm{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(8^2)\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 32 \times \frac{3\pi}{4} = 24\pi\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$ (c) Triangle area: $A_{\mathrm{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(64)\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 16\sqrt{2}\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$ Segment area: $A_{\mathrm{segment}} = A_{\mathrm{sector}} - A_{\mathrm{triangle}} = 24\pi - 16\sqrt{2} = 8(3\pi - 2\sqrt{2})\mathrm{\ cm}^2.$

questions.q: Decompose the rational expression $R(x) = \frac{7x - 1}{x^2 - x - 6}$ into partial fractions using the Heaviside cover-up method.
questions.answer: Step 1: Factor denominator: $x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2).$ Set up the decomposition: $\frac{7x - 1}{(x - 3)(x + 2)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 2}.$ Step 2: Apply Heaviside cover-up method:For $A$ (evaluate at $x = 3$): $A = \left.\frac{7x - 1}{x + 2}\right|_{x=3} = \frac{7(3) - 1}{3 + 2} = \frac{20}{5} = 4.$ For $B$ (evaluate at $x = -2$): $B = \left.\frac{7x - 1}{x - 3}\right|_{x=-2} = \frac{7(-2) - 1}{-2 - 3} = \frac{-15}{-5} = 3.$ The partial fraction decomposition is $\frac{4}{x - 3} + \frac{3}{x + 2}$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Factor denominator: $x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2).$ Set up the decomposition: $\frac{7x - 1}{(x - 3)(x + 2)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 2}.$ Step 2: Apply Heaviside cover-up method:For $A$ (evaluate at $x = 3$): $A = \left.\frac{7x - 1}{x + 2}\right|_{x=3} = \frac{7(3) - 1}{3 + 2} = \frac{20}{5} = 4.$ For $B$ (evaluate at $x = -2$): $B = \left.\frac{7x - 1}{x - 3}\right|_{x=-2} = \frac{7(-2) - 1}{-2 - 3} = \frac{-15}{-5} = 3.$ The partial fraction decomposition is $\frac{4}{x - 3} + \frac{3}{x + 2}$.

questions.q: Evaluate the definite integral $\int_0^{\sqrt{7}} \frac{4x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9}}\,dx$ using the substitution $u = x^2 + 9$.
questions.target: Reading grouped frequency data from a bar chart
questions.answer: 1. Let $u = x^2 + 9$. Then $du = 2x\,dx \Rightarrow 4x\,dx = 2\,du$. 2. Transform the limits of integration: When $x = 0$: $u = 0^2 + 9 = 9$. When $x = \sqrt{7}$: $u = (\sqrt{7})^2 + 9 = 7 + 9 = 16$. 3. Rewrite the integral in terms of $u$: $\int_9^{16} \frac{2}{\sqrt{u}}\,du = 2 \int_9^{16} u^{-1/2}\,du = 2 \left[ 2 u^{1/2} \right]_9^{16} = 4 \left[ \sqrt{u} \right]_9^{16}.$ 4. Evaluate at the boundaries: $4(\sqrt{16} - \sqrt{9}) = 4(4 - 3) = 4(1) = 4.$ The exact value of the integral is 4.
questions.explanation: 1. Let $u = x^2 + 9$. Then $du = 2x\,dx \Rightarrow 4x\,dx = 2\,du$. 2. Transform the limits of integration: When $x = 0$: $u = 0^2 + 9 = 9$. When $x = \sqrt{7}$: $u = (\sqrt{7})^2 + 9 = 7 + 9 = 16$. 3. Rewrite the integral in terms of $u$: $\int_9^{16} \frac{2}{\sqrt{u}}\,du = 2 \int_9^{16} u^{-1/2}\,du = 2 \left[ 2 u^{1/2} \right]_9^{16} = 4 \left[ \sqrt{u} \right]_9^{16}.$ 4. Evaluate at the boundaries: $4(\sqrt{16} - \sqrt{9}) = 4(4 - 3) = 4(1) = 4.$ The exact value of the integral is 4.

questions.q: A surveyor measures distances from an observation point $C$ to two landmarks $A$ and $B$: $AC = 140\mathrm{\ m}$ and $BC = 210\mathrm{\ m}$, with included angle $\angle ACB = 78^\circ$. Find the distance $AB$ between the landmarks to the nearest tenth of a meter, and compute the area of $\Delta  ABC$ to the nearest square meter.
questions.target: Measures of central tendency for grouped data
questions.answer: Apply the Law of Cosines to find side $c = AB$: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C = 210^2 + 140^2 - 2(210)(140)\cos 78^\circ.$ $c^2 = 44100 + 19600 - 58800(0.2079) = 63700 - 12225 = 51475.$ $c = \sqrt{51475} \approx 226.9\mathrm{\ m}.$ Compute the area: $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \frac{1}{2}(210)(140)\sin 78^\circ = 14700(0.9781) \approx 14379\mathrm{\ m}^2.$
questions.explanation: Apply the Law of Cosines to find side $c = AB$: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C = 210^2 + 140^2 - 2(210)(140)\cos 78^\circ.$ $c^2 = 44100 + 19600 - 58800(0.2079) = 63700 - 12225 = 51475.$ $c = \sqrt{51475} \approx 226.9\mathrm{\ m}.$ Compute the area: $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \frac{1}{2}(210)(140)\sin 78^\circ = 14700(0.9781) \approx 14379\mathrm{\ m}^2.$

questions.q: The following bar chart shows the number of students who achieved different grades in a mathematics test. The grades are A, B, C, and D. The data is as follows: Grade A: 14 students, Grade B: 22 students, Grade C: 18 students, Grade D: 26 students. What is the total number of students who took the test?
questions.answer: To find the total number of students who took the test, we need to sum the number of students who achieved each grade. Number of students with Grade A = 14 Number of students with Grade B = 22 Number of students with Grade C = 18 Number of students with Grade D = 26 Total number of students = 14 + 22 + 18 + 26 = 80. Therefore, 80 students took the test.
questions.explanation: To find the total number of students who took the test, we need to sum the number of students who achieved each grade. Number of students with Grade A = 14 Number of students with Grade B = 22 Number of students with Grade C = 18 Number of students with Grade D = 26 Total number of students = 14 + 22 + 18 + 26 = 80. Therefore, 80 students took the test.

Substituting these values into the formula, we get: $22 = 86 - Q_1$ To find $Q_1$, we rearrange the equation: $Q_1 = 86 - 22$ $Q_1 = 64$ Therefore, the first quartile is 64 marks. questions.q: The bar chart below shows the number of students who chose each of four different sports as their favorite. What is the total number of students surveyed?
questions.answer: The bar chart shows the following counts for each sport: Sport 1: 14 students Sport 2: 22 students Sport 3: 18 students Sport 4: 26 students To find the total number of students surveyed, we sum the number of students for each sport: $14 + 22 + 18 + 26$. $14 + 22 = 36$ $18 + 26 = 44$ $36 + 44 = 80$. Therefore, the total number of students surveyed is 80.
